result.title: Collaborative Language Models for Semantic IoT Data Processing: Validation through Zero-Shot Human Activity Recognition
result.summary: Internet of Things (IoT) systems generate low-level sensor observations that are not directly suitable for process analysis and must first be transformed into semantically meaningful events. This paper investigates collaborative language models as a zero-shot semantic abstraction layer for converting such observations into higher-level event and activity labels. We propose a five-stage workflow comprising semantic mapping, semantic aggregation, temporal and contextual aggregation, specialized reasoning, and final event abstraction. The resulting labels and contextual information can subsequently be represented as event records for downstream Process Mining (PM) tasks. The approach is evaluated through Human Activity Recognition on the CASAS Aruba smart home dataset using eleven workflow configurations. The experiments show that collaboration alone does not guarantee improved performance: general-purpose auxiliary SLMs can degrade recognition, whereas assigning complementary specialist roles leads to better results and allows a smaller final classifier to retain much of the performance of a larger model. The selected workflow achieves a macro F1 of 0.643 in the 1.5-day comparison and 0.567 (weighted F1 0.680) in a one-week evaluation. Although trained ML approaches remain more accurate on this dataset, the results demonstrate a different design point: modular semantic event abstraction using off-the-shelf models without task-specific parameter fine-tuning. The findings indicate that the structure of LM collaboration and task decomposition is more important than simply increasing the number of participating models.

AI.brief_summary: 该文将多个语言模型组合为「零样本语义抽象层」，用语义映射、聚合、时序与上下文聚合、专门化推理、事件抽象五个阶段把 IoT 底层传感器观测转换为高层活动标签，并在 CASAS Aruba 智能家居数据上用十一种流程配置评估人类活动识别效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其分阶段语义抽象与「角色互补才增益、单纯增加模型反而变差」的结论，可供核查多级推理状态抽象、角色分工与贡献分配在 LVR 流程中的设计取舍；但场景非视觉、无 latent 状态，迁移性待验证。
